ledger.claim: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The platform's optimal route between the booked pickup and dropoff is 9.4 km; the driver's trace ran 23.86 km, an excess of 14.46 km, which is 153.83% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are passed on any reading: the excess is far greater than 20% of optimal AND far greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms.

The deviation is not merely established but MATERIAL. An excess above 50% of optimal, or above 8.0 km absolute, is material under POL-RD-01; this trip clears both limbs at once (153.83% and 14.46 km). Materiality is the trigger that puts the driver's profile in issue under POL-RD-06 and it is the finding on which the refund computation runs.

The governing distance is the trace figure, not the trip record's convenience copy. POL-RD-01 provides in terms that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs and the rounded trip_record figure may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace records 23.86 km against the trip record's rounded 23.9 km; the trace number is the one to use, and it makes no difference to the result — the excess is material on either figure.

There is no exoneration under POL-RD-03, and the driver's own account cannot supply one. The traffic advisory artifact for this corridor, EV-ADVIS-00504-01, is MISSING: it carries no payload and an admissibility weight of 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and the blocking detail that no advisory covers the PIE eastbound between Paya Lebar and Tampines in this window. I disclose that impairment expressly under POL-GEN-02. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that names the affected segment and has a validity window overlapping the trip; the absence of any advisory is citable and it defeats the clause. The driver's belief that an accident lay ahead, formed from headlights flashing behind him, is not a traffic advisory and does not satisfy the clause's first limb.

POL-RD-04 cannot be invoked, because the detour was not rider-requested. The chat log for this trip, EV-CHAT-00504, is COMPLETE and contains zero messages (message_count 0, first and last message timestamps null, not truncated); the trip record independently records chat_message_count 0. There is therefore no rider instruction, no timestamped waypoint, and no waypoint_hint to corroborate. Nothing in the record attributes the extra 14.46 km to anything the rider asked for.

POL-RD-05 cannot be invoked either: the endpoints were never amended. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null, and original_pickup and original_dropoff both null. There was no pin move, no in-chat address change and no platform-directed bay reassignment, so the re-quote route does not exist and the booked optimal route of 9.4 km is the correct baseline.

The trace carries no impairment under POL-RD-07 and so requires no independent corroboration. Coverage is 100.0%, point_count 229 at a 10-second cadence against an expected 10 seconds, the gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0 — so there is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m, and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The trace is clean for policy purposes and the excess may be measured from it directly.

The rider has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 places on her, and no additional corroboration is demanded of her. The three load-bearing artifacts describe the same trip: EV-TRIP-00504, EV-GPS-00504 and EV-FARE-00504 all carry trip_id TRP-00504, and the trace's first fix at 18:16:40 matches the trip record's started_at. The excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The enhanced-corroboration proviso does not bite either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, well below the threshold of 4, so the extra-source requirement is not engaged.

The remedy is arithmetic and it comes out in the rider's favour. The fare model on this trip is METERED, so POL-RD-02 applies. Taking the fare breakdown's own constants and the booked optimal of 9.4 km and 14.0 min: (3.80 + 0.75 x 9.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 15.57. The rider was charged 33.17, so the refund is 33.17 - 15.57 = 17.60, payable rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 17.60 itself. That is 53.06% of charged_total — above the 0.50 de minimis floor so a refund must issue, and below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 17.60 is the correct outcome, and it is a real return of part of the contested amount to the filing party under POL-GEN-03.

Nothing is added on top of that refund for pass-through lines, and the rider does not overreach by asking for any. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry charges at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0, optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.0), no airport surcharge and no waiting-time fee. Under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would already have been comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation rather than added to it; here there is none, so the SGD 17.60 figure stands as the single, unduplicated amount owed.

I have run the POL-RD-06 profile check that materiality requires, and I state its result honestly: no repeat-deviation pattern is established. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test is met, and the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is not available. The rider's entitlement on this record is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial of SGD 17.60, and no conduct referral follows. I note also that trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 has no application and the 9.4 km solo optimal is the correct baseline.

The rider's practical complaint is borne out by the ledger: she was charged 33.17 for a trip whose optimal-route cost is 15.57, so she paid roughly 2.1 times what the journey was worth on the platform's own model. The driver's stated reason for the detour — a safety decision taken on the strength of another motorist's headlights — is not one of the exculpatory grounds the policy provides, and with no traffic advisory on file and no rider instruction in the chat, the whole of the excess remains unexcused and refundable up to the arithmetic limit POL-RD-02 sets.

ledger.claim: The driver's explanation — high-beam flashes from a car behind him and a belief that an accident lay ahead — is an external-event defence, and on this policy it can only be run through POL-RD-03, which requires a traffic_advisory that names the affected segment and whose validity window overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached it. The only advisory artifact in this pool, EV-ADVIS-00504-01, is IMPAIRED: its admissibility status is MISSING, the issue code fired is MISSING_ARTIFACT, it has no payload and it carries weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no exoneration fact and no capped excess can be computed under POL-RD-03. That is precisely the situation POL-RD-10(5) names in terms — 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' — and it directs that no final monetary ruling issue: the matter must be escalated to a human reviewer with the amount held, not resolved against the driver on a record that is empty where it matters most. Whether the driver's safety judgement was reasonable is the very question the absent advisory would have answered, and a data gap is not a finding for the rider.

However fault is resolved, the money on this trip is arithmetic and the rider's 33.17 figure is not the measure of any award. POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal-route fare as the 3.80 base fare, plus 0.75 x 9.4 optimal km = 7.05 of distance charge, plus 0.28 x 14.0 optimal min = 3.92 of time charge, all at the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown itself, plus the 0.80 platform fee — 15.57 in total, with no ERP, tolls, surcharge, waiting fee or promo to add or subtract. Against a charged_total of 33.17, that puts a ceiling of 17.60 on any distance-and-time refund, not 33.17.

The rider would need a POL-RD-06 pattern to lift a partial refund to a FULL_REFUND or to force a tie-break against the driver, and the driver's own profile shows there is none: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so the count is below the 3-or-more limb and the ratio is 0.00, below the 0.05 limb with at least 40 trips. Neither limb of POL-RD-06 is met, no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) follows, and POL-GEN-01 confines those two fields to that single test — so no other entry on the driver profile, including the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter which is NOT the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for, may ground any adverse finding against him.

ledger.claim: Nothing can be added on top of the recomputation to inflate the award. POL-RD-09(1) makes off-route ERP already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and forbids adding it a second time, and on this trip there is nothing to comprehend in the first place: erp_lines total 0.00, tolls_erp is 0.00, waiting_time_fee is 0.00, and the airport_surcharge line is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. The rider's remedy on this record is therefore bounded by the 17.60 recomputation and by nothing else.

The refund the evidence actually supports is 53.06% of charged_total — 17.60 of 33.17 — which is below the 90% level at which POL-RD-02 converts a partial refund into a FULL_REFUND. The rider's framing that she 'paid nearly three times the normal price' therefore cannot be converted into a full return of the whole contested sum: the outcome available on this record is at most a PARTIAL_REFUND, and the portion the driver keeps is the 15.57 optimal-route fare he genuinely earned plus the platform fee.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver — here is what is settled and what is not, and why this case goes to a human reviewer instead of being paid out or dismissed today.

What is settled. The platform's optimal route between Paya Lebar Square and Tampines MRT is 9.4 km and 14.0 minutes. The GPS trace for the trip records 23.86 km — the trace figure governs over the trip record's rounded 23.9 km under POL-RD-01 — an excess of 14.46 km, or 153.83% of optimal. That clears both establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km absolute) and is a material deviation on this trip's own evidence. The trace is clean for policy purposes: 100% coverage, 229 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps and no jumps, so no independent corroboration is required under POL-RD-07. The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 burden: the trip record, trace and fare breakdown all carry TRP-00504, her profile's deviation_claims_60d is 0, and no extra corroboration is demanded of her. The fare is METERED, and on the fare breakdown's own constants the optimal-route fare would be 3.80 + (0.75 x 9.4) + (0.28 x 14.0) = 15.57 at the 1.0 surge multiplier recorded on that artifact, plus the 0.80 platform fee. Against the 33.17 charged, that is a refund of 17.60 — 53.06% of the charge, above the 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% that would convert it to a full refund. Nothing is added for pass-throughs: ERP, tolls, surcharge, waiting fee and promo are all nil, so POL-RD-09 contributes nothing further. There was no rider-requested detour (the chat log exists and is empty, so POL-RD-04 cannot run), no amended pickup or dropoff (POL-RD-05 cannot run), the vehicle was RYDE_X so POL-RD-12 does not apply, and the fare was not upfront-quoted so POL-RD-11 does not apply. I have also run the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check that materiality requires: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available and no conduct referral follows. Only those two profile fields were used for that test; the lifetime counters such as prior_deviation_flags are context only and grounded no finding.

What is not settled. The driver's explanation is that a car behind him flashed high beams several times near the exit, that he believed an accident lay ahead so he stayed on the expressway, and that he turned back at the next exit — in the rider's account, he said he thought the road was closed. That is an external-event defence, and the only clause that can carry it is POL-RD-03, which requires a traffic_advisory naming the affected segment with a validity window overlapping the trip. The only advisory artifact in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00504-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT and its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0, so it can carry no fact and only its absence is citable (POL-GEN-02(3)). POL-RD-10(5) names precisely this situation — a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory — as one in which no final monetary ruling may issue. The driver's account on its own does not establish a closure: a stated reason records only that it was stated, a record the platform generates is the platform's, and POL-RD-03 reads the advisory rather than the driver's belief, so a general assertion of this kind does not discharge his POL-RD-08 burden. But the absent advisory is a gap in the record, not a finding against him, and the same principle that stops a data failure being turned into a finding for one side stops it being turned into a finding for the other.

Result. The outcome is ESCALATE, which is terminal: no money moves now, both money fields are null, and the disputed 33.17 is held rather than collected or refunded. The rider's arithmetic is not rejected — if the reviewer concludes there was no closure, the POL-RD-02 refund of 17.60 is the figure that follows; if the reviewer concludes the driver's external-event account is made out on a properly produced advisory, exoneration under POL-RD-03 would change that. What would resolve the case is the LTA advisory record for the Paya Lebar–Tampines corridor on the evening of 23 August 2026, or a record confirming that no advisory was issued. My confidence is 0.70, at the platform floor.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
